ambiguities.impact: When all Xᵢ vanish almost surely, the ordinary-real expression c t²/0 is undefined (and is 0/0 at t=0). The probabilistic boundary facts are clear—probability 0 for t>0 and probability 1 for t=0—but the source does not say which arithmetic convention or case split encodes them.
ambiguities.issue: The displayed denominator may be zero although the theorem quantifies over every t ≥ 0.

contract_plain_english: There is an unspecified positive universal constant c such that any finite independent family of mean-zero sub-gaussian real random variables satisfies, for every nonnegative threshold, a two-sided Hoeffding tail bound whose scale is the sum of their squared ψ₂ norms. Here ψ₂ is the exponential-square norm defined by the infimum condition E exp(X²/s²) ≤ 2. The proof uses the equivalent mean-zero MGF bound only up to absolute constants, multiplies MGFs using independence, converts back to ψ₂ control, and invokes the ψ₂ tail estimate. The printed source leaves the zero-denominator case unstated and must not be read as silently excluding it or as choosing a particular MGF variance proxy.

source_evidence.observation: For independent, mean-zero, sub-gaussian X₁,…,X_N and every t ≥ 0, the source states P{|∑ᵢ₌₁ᴺ Xᵢ| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c t²/(∑ᵢ₌₁ᴺ ‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂})).

source_evidence.observation: The proof factors the MGF of ∑Xᵢ by independence, applies (2.16) termwise, sets K² := C∑‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}, converts the resulting MGF control back to ψ₂-norm control using Proposition 2.5.2(v),(iv) and Definition 2.5.6, and then obtains Theorem 2.6.2 from the tail inequality (2.14).

binders: A positive integer N (implicit in the notation X₁,…,X_N).
Real-valued random variables X₁,…,X_N on a common probability space.
A real threshold t with t ≥ 0.
definitions_and_conventions: The sub-gaussian norm is ‖X‖_{ψ₂} := inf{s > 0 : E exp(X²/s²) ≤ 2}, i.e. the scale associated with Proposition 2.5.2(iv).
The symbol c denotes a positive absolute (universal) constant, not a theorem input and not a specified numerical value; the book's equivalences permit absolute constant factors.
The absolute value is outside the whole sum, so the claim is a two-sided tail bound.

The theorem is formulated in ψ₂ norms. The mean-zero MGF estimate E exp(λX) ≤ exp(Cλ²‖X‖²_{ψ₂}) for all λ ∈ ℝ is an equivalent property used in the proof, not a replacement statement with a separately fixed variance/MGF parameter.
hypotheses: Each Xᵢ has mean zero: E Xᵢ = 0.
Each Xᵢ is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6 / Proposition 2.5.2.
implicit_context: All probabilities and expectations refer to the common underlying probability space.
The same absolute-constant convention used in (2.14)–(2.16) and Proposition 2.6.1 is inherited by the theorem.
The source states the inequality for every t ≥ 0 without separately assuming ∑ᵢ ‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂} > 0 or declaring an extended-real division convention.

details: The bound is uniform over N, all families satisfying the three hypotheses, and all t ≥ 0.
Its concentration rate is controlled by the sum of the squared ψ₂ norms, up to one absolute constant c.
Mean zero permits the ψ₂-to-MGF estimate (2.16), yielding exp(λ²K²) with K² = C∑‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}.
Proposition 2.5.2(v)⇔(iv) and Definition 2.5.6 convert this MGF estimate to ψ₂-norm control of the sum; the tail form (2.14) then gives the displayed theorem.

details: If every ψ₂ norm is zero, the printed denominator vanishes.
The source nevertheless includes t = 0 and supplies neither a positive-denominator side condition nor a convention for t²/0, so the literal displayed quotient has an unstated boundary interpretation.

undebatable_constraints: Retain mutual independence, individual mean-zero assumptions, and sub-gaussianity of every summand.
Retain the two-sided event |∑Xᵢ| ≥ t and the universal range t ≥ 0.
Retain the denominator ∑ᵢ‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}; do not replace it by a chosen MGF proxy, variance, maximum norm, or unweighted count.
Retain the source's unspecified absolute-constant convention: c is universal and positive, not a fixed numeric constant silently selected by the formalizer.

Do not silently remove the all-zero family or t = 0. Because the source does not specify division by a zero denominator, a formal statement must expose how that boundary case is represented rather than pretending the printed real quotient is already defined there.
Preserve the source proof route as ψ₂-norm/MGF equivalence up to absolute constants, rather than recasting the theorem as one tied to a particular MGF parameterization.
